history.dynasty: Lodhi-era; built by the Nawab of Sultanpur Lodhi (verify - per local accounts)
history.summary: AMBIGUITY FLAG: 'Shiv Mandir' is a generic name and Jalandhar has several; the most prominent documented one is the historic Shiv Mandir at Gur Mandi, in the heart of the old city's busy market, adjacent to the mosque of Imam Nasar (verify exact adjacency). Per local accounts (pilgrimaide, holyshrines) this is one of the most ancient temples of the Jalandhar region, dating to the Lodhi era and built by a Nawab who ruled Jalandhar (one account says the Nawab of Sultanpur Lodhi). Its legend: a Nawab coveted a newly married Hindu woman, a devotee of Shiva; a serpent saved her honour, and the repentant Nawab built the temple at her bidding. Its architecture is a noted Hindu-Muslim blend - the front gate in classic Muslim style, the rest of the complex in Hindu style, with white-and-red etched pyramid-shaped shikharas - and it is presented as a living witness of religious tolerance. The Lodhi-era dating and Nawab story rest on travel/pilgrimage sources rather than scholarly ones (verify). If the CSV intends a different Jalandhar Shiv Mandir (e.g. one of the many neighbourhood shrines listed in map directories), this identification should be corrected.

name: Shiv Mandir
town_description: Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, with roots in the Indus Valley Civilization period, and today a major sports-goods and industrial centre. Gur Mandi is the old city's bustling market quarter, home to historic shrines including this Shiva temple.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~80 km); Adampur domestic airport is closer (~25 km, limited service - verify).
travel.railway: Jalandhar City Junction on the Delhi-Amritsar line; Gur Mandi is in the old city, a short auto/rickshaw ride.
travel.road: On NH-44 (Grand Trunk Road); well connected to Amritsar (80 km), Ludhiana (60 km) and Delhi (375 km).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivaratri for the festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listings for similarly named Jalandhar shrines give roughly 5:00/5:30 AM to 9:00/9:15 PM daily (verify - the Gur Mandi temple's own hours are not published; confirm locally).
